question: What is a special feature of the new 'Agni-Prime' missile tested by India in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Canister launch and new materials**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Agni-Prime** is an advanced variant of the Agni series of ballistic missiles developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** in India.
 
• The missile uses **canister-based launch technology**, which allows for easier transportation and quick deployment, significantly enhancing its operational flexibility and reducing response time.
 
• It incorporates the use of **cutting-edge composite materials** in its construction, making it lighter, more efficient, and improving its range and accuracy.
 
• Agni-Prime has a range of **1,000 to 2,000 kilometers**, making it a medium-range ballistic missile suitable for addressing regional security needs.
 
• It is equipped with advanced guidance and navigation systems, ensuring **pinpoint accuracy** and precision targeting, which enhances its effectiveness in strategic missions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Development of Agni-Prime:**

 
 
• The **Agni-Prime** missile is part of India's integrated guided missile development programme (IGMDP), under which various missiles like Agni, Prithvi, and others have been developed.
 
• It is a **canisterised missile**, which means it can be launched from a sealed canister, allowing for better storage, mobility, and quick launch capabilities.
 
• The missile is a lighter and more efficient version of the Agni-I and Agni-II missiles, with enhanced features for strategic deterrence.
 
 
 
• **Features of Canister Launch:**
 
 
• Canister launching provides the advantage of **mobility** and reduces the time needed for launch preparations.
 
• It allows the missile to be pre-fueled and stored for extended periods, enhancing the missile system's reliability and readiness.
 
• The canister protects the missile from environmental conditions and increases its shelf life.
 
 
 
• **Importance of New Materials:**
 
 
• Agni-Prime uses lightweight **composite materials** that improve its overall performance by reducing weight and enhancing fuel efficiency.
 
• The advanced materials increase the missile’s structural strength and its ability to withstand high temperatures and pressures during flight.
 
• The use of cutting-edge materials also reduces the cost of production while maintaining the missile's reliability and effectiveness.
 
 
 
• **Advanced Features:**
 
 
• Agni-Prime is equipped with state-of-the-art **navigation and guidance systems**, which ensure high precision in hitting targets.
 
• The missile has a **dual-stage engine**, making it more efficient and providing it with a longer range compared to its predecessors.
 
• It is capable of carrying a variety of **warheads** and has high maneuverability, making it a versatile component of India’s defense arsenal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Agni Missile Series:**

 
 
• The Agni missile series is a family of medium to intercontinental range ballistic missiles developed by the **DRDO** of India under the IGMDP.
 
• The series includes Agni-I, Agni-II, Agni-III, Agni-IV, Agni-V, and now Agni-Prime.
 
• Agni-V is India’s longest-range ballistic missile, with a range of over 5,000 kilometers, capable of carrying nuclear warheads.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The Agni series strengthens India’s **deterrence capability** and bolsters its defense against potential external threats.
 
• The enhanced features of Agni-Prime make it a crucial element in India’s strategy of credible minimum deterrence and no-first-use policy.
 
 
 
• **Canister-Based Systems:**
 
 
• Canister-based missile systems provide a significant edge in terms of quick deployment and mobility during conflict scenarios.
 
• Such systems are particularly useful for maintaining an effective second-strike capability.
